Hi, Chris,

Thanks for your information.



1, Yes, DC57V(DC56.6V) is good to do stable operation and PoE output(double
confirmed with our engineer)



2, About the DC75V drawing, it is a common description.

If you look at the Non-PoE model, it is also this drawing.

We simply use the same side panel, so there is DC75V.

But the power input for PoE models should be DC44V~DC57V.



3, About SNMP function, please see attached file and confirm if it is OK
for your system.

Please let us know if you need extra features not listed there.

We will see what we can do.



4, About this model, is it L2+ or L3?

Then I will quote.



Thank you.

Hi Alan,

Thank you for the details.

I am interested in something like a STI-41616XGGPM-4BT

Can you confirm that it will work up to at least 57V DC? your manual 
says 57V, but the Mechanical/CAD drawing says 75V.

I would be running it on a 48V LiFePO4 system, which at peak voltage 
will be 56.6V

I recently bought a LinoVision switch (similar industrial format) which 
claims it works up to 57V, but in reality, when it gets to 56.xV it 
seems to reboot itself, which is really annoying.

Also, is SNMP support reliable? The LinoVision gives really random and 
therefore useless values for bandwidth usage, and their support seems to 
be unhelpful in fixing the problem.

How much would one cost including shipping to the UK?

Thank you,

Chris
